facts.statement: Judiceratops is an extinct horned dinosaur whose name means "Judith River horned face".
facts.quote: Judiceratops ( ; meaning "Judith River horned face") is an extinct horned dinosaur.

facts.statement: Judiceratops was a large, four-legged herbivore like other horned dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Like other horned dinosaurs, Judiceratops was a large, quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Judiceratops is the oldest known member of the chasmosaurine subgroup of horned dinosaurs.
facts.quote: It is the oldest known chasmosaurine.

facts.statement: Judiceratops had moderately long postorbital horns that pointed forward and outward with an unusual teardrop-shaped cross-section.
facts.quote: The postorbital (located above the eyes) horns are moderately elongate, inclined forward and outwards, and have an unusual teardrop-shaped cross section.

facts.statement: Judiceratops possessed large scallops on the inner edges of its frill and a very broad, plate-like bar in the center of the frill.
facts.quote: It shows that the animal had large scallops on the frill's proximal margins, and a very broad, platelike bar in the center of the frill.

facts.statement: The bony projections on the side edges of Judiceratops' frill were large near the front but became small toward the back.
facts.quote: The osteoderms on the lateral margins of the frill are large near the front, but small towards the back.

facts.statement: Judiceratops is classified as a basal member of the chasmosaurine subfamily.
Researchers suggest that the rapid evolution of frill features in horned dinosaurs, including Judiceratops, was driven by sexual selection.
facts.quote: This probably reflects rapid evolution of the frill in response to sexual selection, similar to how sexual selection creates a large variety of display feathers in living dinosaurs such as birds of paradise.

facts.statement: Judiceratops is the oldest known chasmosaurine and already displays distinctive group features like long, concave squamosals and pointed epioccipitals.
facts.quote: Judiceratops is the oldest known member of the Chasmosaurinae, but already shows many of the distinctive features of the group including the long, concave squamosals and pointed epioccipitals.

facts.statement: No fossils of the Judiceratops lineage are known from later rocks, suggesting a pattern of rapid evolution and extinction common in late Cretaceous horned dinosaurs.
facts.quote: No fossils from this lineage are known from later rocks, consistent with a pattern of high turnover- species rapidly evolved, and became extinct- as seen in other horned dinosaurs in the latest Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Judiceratops was recovered from the Judith River Formation in Hill County, Montana.
facts.quote: The remains of the holotype specimen of Judiceratops YPM VPPU 022404 were recovered from the Judith River Formation in Hill County, Montana.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Judiceratops is currently housed at the Yale Peabody Museum.
facts.quote: This specimen is housed at the Yale Peabody Museum.

facts.statement: Judiceratops shared its environment with bony fishes, amphibians, Champsosaurus, Brachylophosaurus canadensis, Colepiocephale lambei, Dromaeosaurus, Gorgosaurus, Troodon, Albertaceratops, Medusaceratops, and Avaceratops.
facts.quote: Judiceratops shared its paleoenvironment with bony fishes, amphibians, the Choristoderan Champsosaurus, the hadrosaur Brachylophosaurus canadensis, the pachycephalosaur Colepiocephale lambei, the theropods Dromaeosaurus, Gorgosaurus and Troodon, and with fellow ceratopsians Albertaceratops, Medusaceratops and Avaceratops.

facts.statement: Judiceratops tigris is the only known species of the extinct Judiceratops genus, living between 78 and 77 million years ago during the middle Campanian in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Judiceratops tigris es la única especie conocida del género extinto Judiceratops de dinosaurio ceratópsido, que vivió a finales del Cretácico, hace entre 78 y 77 millones de años , durante el Campaniense medio, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The holotype YPM VPPU 022404 consists of an incomplete skull including postorbital horns, parts of the frontal, prefrontal, and lacrimal bones, the right squamosal, parietals, occipital condyle, and parts of the supraoccipital.
facts.quote: El holotipo YPM VPPU 022404 consiste en un cráneo incompleto el cual incluye los cuernos postorbitales, partes de los frontales, prefrontales y lacrimales, partes del escamosal derecho y los parietales, el cóndilo occipital y partes del supraoccipital.

facts.statement: Judiceratops is a basal member of the Chasmosaurinae subfamily.
The time range for Judiceratops is recorded as the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: It lived around 78 million years ago, during the Late Cretaceous Period in what is now Montana, United States.
